The added code checks if a source is already in the scene when adding existing sources. If so, nothing will be done except for a log warning.
The reason for not renaming is that I have noticed that flag `OBS_SOURCE_DO_NOT_DUPLICATE` may be set for sources, so that 
duplicating and renaming may not be proper.

Also, though no change is done to `/UI/window-basic-source-select.cpp` during this commit, I doubt that line 166 at: /UI/window-basic-source-select.cpp, namely
```cpp
obs_source_release(source);
```
It may should be 
```cpp
obs_source_release(from);
```
as `source` is newly created from `obs_source_duplicate`.

body:
The root cause of name conflicts in the scene item list probably lies in the fact that scene item uses name of its source as its name while scene items are allowed to have the same source. It should be noted that sources themselves have checked unique names, but more than one scene items are using the name of one source. 

The simplest approach is to prevent scene items from using the same source, as it was in my last pr. But it is pointed out that users will not expect this, while you cannot duplicate sources directly sometimes, so the only approach is to add independent
name property for scene items. But this involves bunches of parts in, like releasing memory usage, which may cause further problems, and i'm confusing about it. 

In the current version, name of scene item is name of its source. So in most cases, when you get name of scene item, `obs_source_get_name(item->source)` is used. When you rename scene item, you rename the source, then other scene items using the same source. Adding independent name property for scene items means you leave name of sources away, which is nonsense.

### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail. -->
<!--- If this change includes UI elements, please include screenshots. -->
As is explained in my comment at [issue #5621](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/issues/5621), my resolution is to add an independent property for scene items. And because it involves many parts in, finally I store it in `item->private_settings` to prevent memory allocating & releasing issues. 
(see `obs_sceneitem_set_itemname` and more).

Generally, after modification, when you add an existing source, arg `existing` will be set `true` at `obs_scene_add_internal`, thus leading to searching for a new name. On the other side, when you rename scene items, you will never rename source itself but only "item_name" of scene items. **New name property will only be shown on source list and context bar.** 

Also, there are 2 main bold changes that I'm worrying about. 

One is changes in properties of `struct AddSourceData` and arguments of `obs_scene_add_internal` & `obs_scene_add`. I found it hard to directly set "item_name" in function `AddExisting` at windows-basic-source-select.cpp and above, so I add arg & property instead to ask for a new name.

The other is line 539 at source-tree.cpp. Although renaming sources directly is stopped, you can still rename sources in mixer, which leads to incorrect labels changes in source list of scene. As I cannot think of a better idea to stop it, I stopped it at line 539 directly.

Detailed explanation is attached.

body:
I didn't expect that name conflicts in source list would be intentional, so i totally mistook the point last time. The problem is specific to global audio sources.

Now i suppose the point is, it is expected that if you disable the global audio source on settings windows, it should be removed on spot, while the fact is that, if you add scene items using global audio source, you add **extra strong reference** to it thus leading to its not being removed. On the other hand, changing from "disabled" to some available source directly causes creation of new source, so there are name conflicts.

There are 2 main solutions for solving the problem. One is removing scene items using the global audio sources when disabling, the other is checking reference count to decide if permitting "disabled". For the moment i tend to the latter solution, and i have 3 plans to push it:

1. checking refs on `SaveAudioSettings`
2. checking refs on `AudioChanged`
3. checking refs on `LoadListValues`

All 3 plans requires a copy of value of refs of source directly. Currently i'm working on the third plan.

body: After thinking about this, my preference would be that changing the device in Settings would simply update the property for the global source, rather than destroying and recreating the source entirely. This would also fix other sections such as Hotkeys reloading 3 times when the audio device is changed.

I checked code related to the process and suppose it is `OBSBasic::ResetAudioDevice` at UI/window-basic-main.cpp.
Changing from one available audio source to another seems to just update settings for the source, while changing from one aviable audio source to "disabled" , then to another available one seems to destroy & recreate it. So perhaps preventing global audio source in use from being disabled will prevent the extra process in the same time.

@jp9000 Well, i could have drawn it from the fact that obs lib has no direct access to the reference number. It depends on whether you want to keep it 'global'. Btw, there's a similar function `get_new_source_name` in frontend/windows-basic-source-select.cpp, and i suppose it may cause some harmless duplication.
